entries.proposition: Framing: the paper states, in its Introduction, that stiripentol is an inhibitor of lactate dehydrogenase, citing a review; the sentence is a statement of the literature and carries no measurement of this paper.
entries.snippet: inhibitor of the neoglucogenesis enzyme named lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), which is highly activated during seizures

entries.proposition: Aim and design: the work set out to measure both stiripentol enantiomers against human LDHA for the first time and to test four newly made stiripentol-related compounds; the target is the recombinant human LDHA isoform, not a brain preparation.
entries.snippet: we have proposed, in the present work, the evaluation of the inhibitory activity of both STP enantiomers

entries.proposition: Screening result for stiripentol and iso-stiripentol: at a single concentration of 500 micromolar, racemic stiripentol, its two enantiomers and iso-stiripentol inhibited human LDHA by 10 to 38 percent, whereas the four analogues tested reached 46 to 72 percent. This is a single-concentration screen, not a potency.
entries.snippet: showed low percentages of inhibition (10–38%), whereas significant values (46–72% of inhibition) were achieved for compounds

entries.proposition: Potency claim and its limit: the authors write that the analogues' IC50 values are 100 to 200 micromolar; Table 2 spans 101.7 to 213.7 (one value, 213.7, lies outside the rounded range) and the racemate-versus-enantiomer scatter inside the series is up to two-fold (see the Table 2 entries). Stiripentol and iso-stiripentol are described as 'higher than 500 micromolar': for stiripentol this is a bound, and no dose-response curve is reported for it (the supplement's curves S65 to S74 cover analogues only; the Results say the IC50 phase was run for compounds with notable activity, 3 to 5). That stiripentol had no curve run is an inference from those two places, because the Table 2 footnote b sits on the whole IC50 column. The word 'significantly' carries no statistical test in the text.
entries.snippet: All these novel compounds showed IC50 values in the range of 100–200 µM, significantly improving the activity shown by 1 and 2 (with IC50 values higher than 500 µM)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: AUDIT (disease-models/wwox/research/locator_audits/2026-10-27_PMID39769031_blind_audit.md, scientist-d): range stated as 100-200 although Table 2 is 101.7-213.7; 'only a single-concentration percentage was measured' narrowed to 'no curve reported', an inference.

entries.proposition: The lowest IC50 in the series is (-)-(2R,5S)-4 at 101.7 micromolar; the authors place it beside galloflavin (103.6) and luteolin-7-O-glucoside (139.2), i.e. a weak tool-grade LDHA inhibitor. Its rank is inside the series scatter: its own racemate, (+/-)-(2S*,5R*)-4, is 199.8, about twice as weak, so it is not established as the best compound. Enantiomers within a pair are described by the authors as not remarkably different.
entries.snippet: enantiomer (−)-(2R,5S)-4 showed the lowest IC50 value (101.7 µM)

contradicts_locator.what_changed: AUDIT (disease-models/wwox/research/locator_audits/2026-10-27_PMID39769031_blind_audit.md, scientist-d): quote supported; caveat added that the series racemate scatter equals the 100-200 band, so 'strongest' is not a ranking.

entries.proposition: What this paper says of the 2015 report (secondary statement only): the authors write that Sada et al. measured stiripentol on purified mammalian LDH, found about 40 percent inhibition of both directions at 500 micromolar, and that this paper found about 10 percent at the same concentration, which they attribute to assay conditions. The 2015 article itself was not read; this sentence is the only description of its numbers in the reading.
entries.snippet: They found that STP, at a concentration of 500 μM, inhibited the lactate-to-pyruvate conversion as well as the pyruvate-to-lactate conversion by approximately 40%.

entries.proposition: Assay conditions for human LDHA: recombinant human LDHA (Abcam), 0.041 units per mL, 155 micromolar NADH, 1 mM pyruvate described as saturating, compound in 5 percent DMSO, 28 degrees C, fluorescence of NADH, GSK2837808A at 1 micromolar as positive control. A saturating pyruvate level is a condition under which a non-competitive or weak inhibitor is detected differently from physiological substrate levels; no detergent is named in the Methods.
entries.snippet: 0.041 units/mL LDHA, 155 μM β-NADH, 1 mM pyruvate (saturated conditions), and DMSO solutions (5%, v/v) of pure compounds

entries.proposition: Replication as printed in the Table 2 footnotes: percentages are n = 4 at a single concentration of 500 micromolar; IC50 values are n = 3 evaluated at eight concentrations spanning 0.46 to 1000 micromolar. The Methods say instead that all measurements were made in triplicate (an internal tension). No independent enzyme lot or second assay format is described (absence claim on Methods 3.10).
entries.snippet: a Percentage of inhibition values are presented as the mean ± SD of n = 4 replicates at a single concentration of 500 μM. b IC50 values are presented as the mean ± SD of n = 3 replicates, evaluated at eight different concentrations, in a range of 0.46–1000 μM.
entries.anchor: Table 2, footnotes a and b (and Methods 3.10 for the triplicate statement)

entries.proposition: Scope of the conclusion: the Conclusions describe inhibition of hLDHA as 'already validated as a safe therapeutic method' for primary hyperoxaluria (liver, a different disease and organ) and say the analogues must still be compared in vivo. No neuronal, brain, seizure, cell or animal experiment exists in this paper (absence claim; the words cell, in vivo and rats also occur outside experiments: Introduction, references, 'quartz cells', 'in vivo' as future work in 2.4 and 4. Conclusions, and rats in 2.4 citing another study; none is an experiment of this paper). The hepatotoxicity caveat is a separate sentence in section 2.4 (next entry).
entries.snippet: the inhibition of hLDHA has already been validated as a safe therapeutic method to treat primary hyperoxaluria (PH)

entries.proposition: Table 2, stiripentol row: racemic stiripentol 9.9 plus or minus 2.3 percent inhibition at 500 micromolar and an IC50 entry of greater than 500.

Table 2, enantiomer rows: (-)-(S)-stiripentol 34.0 plus or minus 2.1 and (+)-(R)-stiripentol 38.4 plus or minus 1.6 percent at 500 micromolar (n = 4), against 9.9 for the racemate and 21.1 for iso-stiripentol. The racemate is below both enantiomers in the same assay and the text does not discuss it (the authors cite only 'ca. 10%' for stiripentol). INFERENCE, not quoted: for a 1:1 mixture of non-interacting equipotent inhibitors the mixture is expected between its components, so this suggests between-preparation or between-run variation. The same racemate-outside-enantiomers pattern recurs in the analogue IC50 data (next entries), in both directions. The enantiomer values (34 to 38) are close to the ~40 percent the authors attribute to the 2015 report; the 10 percent is the racemate only.

entries.proposition: Table 2, analogue rows: racemic compound 3 125.3 plus or minus 19.0 (more potent than both its enantiomers, 213.7 and 166.3); racemic (2S*,5R*)-4 199.8 plus or minus 23.8 (weaker than both its enantiomers, 101.7 plus or minus 6.7 and 128.4 plus or minus 12.4). Racemate and enantiomers differ by up to about two-fold in either direction, so unexplained racemate-versus-enantiomer differences (cause not determined) are about as large as the 100-200 micromolar band separating best from worst analogue: the table reads as a screen, not a ranking.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Figures S65 to S67, page 44 of the supplement read as an image: dose-response curves of compound (+/-)-3, (-)-(S)-3 and (+)-(R)-3 against human LDHA with IC50 125.3, 213.7 and 166.3 micromolar. The curves are steep: for S65 and S67 activity stays near 100 percent to about 30 to 40 micromolar and falls to about 10 percent by about 300, roughly one log unit; S66 falls from about 90 to about 18 percent in about half a log unit. One or two points define each slope, so the Hill slope is unconstrained by the data and is not reported. With 5 percent DMSO and no detergent named, a steep curve is a pattern that also occurs with non-specific or aggregating inhibitors; this is a flag for the analogue series, not a finding. The supplement carries no curve for stiripentol.

entries.proposition: The hepatotoxicity caveat: the authors state, in section 2.4 and not in the Conclusions, that the potential hepatotoxicity of the stiripentol analogues should be evaluated, and cite adverse hepatobiliary reports for stiripentol itself. No safety datum exists in the paper. The paper also cites a hepatoprotective effect of stiripentol on acetaminophen hepatotoxicity in rats (reference 60) and states that the stiripentol label does not currently indicate liver injury, so the caveat runs in both directions.
entries.snippet: the potential hepatotoxicity of these STP analogues should be evaluated
